Independent derivation of the first integral, total density and fixed-bias limit
correctness.rationale: At fixed finite degree z, a dependency path of length n must have n+1 strictly decreasing iid continuous times. Its union bound is z(z−1)^(n−1)/(n+1)! and tends to zero; countability gives simultaneous almost-sure construction. Conditioning on the root's own proposal makes its branches independent with the parent absent. Thus the cavity absence probabilities u=1−a and v=1−b satisfy u' = −p v^(z−1), v' = −q u^(z−1) with u(0)=v(0)=1, and full-root acceptance rates are p v^z and q u^z. The derivative of p v^z−q u^z is zero, giving the stated imbalance. Also (uv)'=−p v^z−q u^z, so total occupation is 1−uv. At balance u=v, and the scalar equation gives the displayed z=2 exponential and z>2 power law, with terminal asymptotic 2 log(z/2)/z. For fixed δ=p−q>0, p v^z=δ+q u^z and v≤1 give u(1)≤1−δ. Changing the minority integral to r=u^z gives zρ_B(1)=∫(q/p) r^(1/z)((δ+qr)/p)^(−(z−1)/z) dr from u(1)^z to 1. The lower endpoint tends to zero and the integrand extended by zero is bounded by q/δ, with pointwise limit q/(δ+qr) for r>0. Integrating gives log(p/δ); symmetry handles the other bias and p=0,1 are trivial. This is an infinite-volume proof, not a fit to the finite-depth simulation.
residual_risks: The large-degree asymptotic is not uniform as p approaches 1/2. The law is a one-point occupation probability for a one-shot tree process, not a finite cyclic graph, repeated trials, or a joint cluster law.

evidence: The exact Penrose–Sudbury blocking theorem is for iid uniform vertex clocks. Meyfroyt uses active-neighbor counts to block a single kind of activation. The pretreatment Bethe-lattice study concerns competitively depositing monomers and dimers on a partially covered tree, rather than alternating one-shot site mark probabilities.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The cavity factorization is known and adapts to alternating hazards, but neither the homogeneous theorem nor these other models directly gives the biased invariant or the minority asymptotic. In the reviewed model the rates alternate because of parity, not because the neighbor degree changes or because a second object occupies an edge.

evidence: Repeated proposals on the lattice admit previously rejected sites again, and the reported rare-species formula is q/(z+1)+O(q²) at small q. The line exact formula implies the imbalance at z=2; the known monomer formula implies balance at any z. Neither passage gives an alternating-clock nonzero-bias invariant or a fixed-bias z→∞ evaluation.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Agreement in a dilute expansion is not domination at fixed p>1/2. To obtain the sharp log(p/(2p−1)) coefficient one needs the biased invariant and a uniform integral bound at fixed bias when taking the degree limit; those are not consequences of the inspected homogeneous result or line law alone.

evidence: Do Amaral–dos Santos uses the same species proposal and blocking rule at z=2. Penrose–Sudbury gives homogeneous nearest-neighbor one-shot monomer RSA on the (k+1)-regular tree with full-root vacancy α(s)=(1+β(s)^2)/2 and β(s)=[1+(k−1)s]^(−1/(k−1)) (or exp(−s) at k=1).
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Xor the species bit with vertex parity: now only equal transformed colors exclude. Each transformed color separately is ordinary monomer RSA with attempts thinned by alternating probabilities p and q; their two marginal processes are not jointly independent. At p=q=1/2 each marginal is exactly homogeneous monomer RSA at s=t/2. Doubling 1−α(t/2), with k=z−1, gives the stated balanced law and ensuing large-degree asymptotic. Off balance, the alternating distributions do not reduce to homogeneous RSA by a common time change.

originality.rationale: The originality supported for the combined finding is the arbitrary-bias regular-tree characterization with its signed-density invariant and sharp fixed-bias minority limit. The line law is previously established. The balanced all-degree closed form and its elementary degree asymptotic are also covered by homogeneous monomer RSA via an exact parameter reduction, and must not be credited independently as new.

No inspected statement was found to establish the combined biased invariant and limiting coefficient. Publisher-specific versions and the cited emptiness article were not inspected in full.

checked_sources: Independent cavity invariant and integral limit; full-text one-shot line, homogeneous regular-tree and retry comparisons above
value.rationale: On the natural regular-tree extension of the one-shot line model, the signed invariant identifies precisely how much of the majority bias survives blocking, and the positive logarithmic coefficient resolves the smaller minority density at fixed bias. Together they distinguish order-one total density at nonzero fixed bias from vanishing balanced density and separate this effect from the different rare-minority retry regime. Value does not rely on the already covered balanced formula.
residual_risks: No quantitative crossover in the coupled limit p→1/2 and z→∞, graph-universality result, or cluster result follows.
